title: Assembly of a miniature two-photon microscope headpiece
protocol: Clean all custom machined components with 95% alcohol in an ultrasonic cleaner at approximately 50°C for 30 minutes.
Air clean all components cleaned in Step 1 in a super clean bench.
Carefully check all components under a stereoscope to ensure they are free from dust and fragments.
Peel off the coating layer (~3 cm) at the end of the HC-920 fiber using a fiber stripping tool.
Cut the end face of the HC-920 fiber using a fiber cutter.
Insert the processed end of the fiber into the glass fiber holder until approximately 1 mm length of fiber appears from the other end.
Drop one drop of UV-Curing optical adhesive to the hopper-like gap at one end of the glass holder.
Wait for 1~2 minutes until the adhesive fills the gap between the glass and the fiber.
Use a UV lamp to solidify the adhesive gel (about 80 seconds exposure).
Monitor the filling of the adhesive under the stereoscope to avoid contaminating the fiber output with the adhesive.
Attach the collimating lens to the collimator holder using a UV-Curing optical adhesive following a similar protocol as in Step 5.
After inserting the fiber holder into the collimator holder, fix the later to an adjustable fiber clamp on a 3-axis stage.
Attach the HC-920 fiber to another adjustable fiber clamp on another 3-axis stage.
Ensure that the HC-920 fiber can move back and forward smoothly within the hole of the fiber holder by adjusting two 3-axis stages coordinately.

Carefully adjust the distance between the end of the fiber (stuck to the fiber holder) and the collimating lens (stuck to the collimator holder) using the adjusters of the 3-axis stage until the laser beam from the collimating lens is collimated.
Monitor the laser beam continuously with the NIR detector card until the center spot remains unchanged within a long distance.
Firmly attach the collimator holder to the fiber holder using UV-Curing optical adhesive.
Prepare the assembling setups as shown in Fig. 2a.
Assemble the objective lens, dichroic mirror, and scan lens to the main frame of the objective in sequence by using UV-Curing optical adhesive.
Attach the upper edge of the objective to the locating ring designed in the main frame so that the distance between the objective lower surface and the main frame surface is approximately 1 mm.
Rotate the reflection-coating surface to face the laser input under the stereoscope.
Insert the dichroic mirror into the narrow slit on the main frame carefully to avoid damaging the surface coating.
Insert the fiber collimator to the main frame and fixing it with a M1.5 screw.
Prepare the alignment setups as shown in Fig. 3.
Pre-align four irises to ensure they are of the same height and collinear to each other.
Fix the main body of the microscope headpiece to the microscope-alignment holder by using a M4 screw.
Switch on the laser.
Remove the 6-Axis kinematic optic mount that holds the microscope-alignment holder.
Observe the laser spot using the NIR Detector Card until the laser beam penetrates through the first pair of collinear irises.
Rotate the main body of the microscope headpiece to ensure its side-face is horizontal.
Re-install the 6-Axis kinematic optic mount that holds the MEMS-alignment holder.
Attach the MEMS onto the MEMS-alignment holder using double-sided tape.
Plug the connected wires of the MEMS onto the PCB attached to the back of the MEMS.
Adjust the MEMS to its center position.
Observe the laser spot after the MEMS with the NIR Detector Card.
Adjust the 6-Axis kinematic optic mount that holds the MEMS-alignment holder until the laser spot becomes the brightest, measured by the power meter.
Keep the MEMS at its center position (zero scanning angle).
Observe the spot of laser reflected from the MEMS with the NIR Detector Card.
Adjust the 6-Axis kinematic optic mount that holds the MEMS-alignment holder until the laser beam penetrates through the second pair of collinear irises.
Move the one-axis stage that holds the MEMS forward to the main body of the microscope headpiece until they almost touch each other.
Adjust the relative position between the MEMS and the main body of the microscope headpiece while observing the laser output from the objective lens.
Ensure the profile of the output laser from the objective is an ellipse symmetrical to the optics axis of the objective for perfect alignment.
Scan the MEMS and observe changes in the direction of the laser from the objective.
Adjust the MEMS position slightly to ensure stable brightness of the laser during scanning.
Repeat steps until both requirements are satisfied.
Drop UV-Curing optical adhesive into the gap between the MEMS package and the surface of the main frame.
Follow the protocol shown in Step 5 for applying the adhesive.
Wait at least 24 hours after curing the UV-Curing optical adhesive to add epoxy glue around the gap.
Attach the collection lens to the end of the SFB before inserting them to the main body of the microscope headpiece.
